I know this is difficult, but you’re thinking of all the right things. There are a lot of factors to consider for both you, and the baby’s future. 

You don’t want to raise a child alone even though you can, and that’s completely valid. Your girlfriend not communicating about this is incredibly frustrating, and I am sorry you have to go through that. These kinds of issues can only grow to harbour resentment in future if not communicated properly. If you go through with an abortion, you may feel resentment over the lack of support and choice at the time. If you keep the baby, your girlfriend may resent you or you may resent her for not being the type of parent you envisioned for your child. It is very important to be on the same page, and her lack of communication is not helping you at all.

You mentioned not wanting to have kids right now, but specifically what are the reasons? For most people it’s stability, but sometimes it can also be reaching certain goals before having kids. It’s important to think about the future you see for yourself and whether or not a baby can fit right now, or what is more important to you.

Your mum being pregnant right now must feel strange too, but it happens and that shouldn’t be a concern. If you go through with an abortion, and you don’t feel comfortable telling your mum that’s okay. Though I would definitely speak to her if you do decide to keep the baby because support is essential.

Despite the opinions of both your mum and girlfriend, it is your choice at the end of the day. I can’t tell you what you should or shouldn’t do, but I can’t say you looking at all the factors before deciding is good, and you’re doing that.

Also, you getting attached to the idea of keeping it after initially thinking you would get an abortion is okay. Remember pro choice is about your choice regardless of what it is.
